Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

koine (development version)

  • The package has a logo.
  • README lists related packages and carries check, coverage and r-universe badges.
  • CI runs lintr (report-only) and test coverage.

koine 0.3.1

  • The package vignette, now titled A second opinion for a mixed model, was restructured to the orchestra’s vignette quality bar: a stated question, a fixed Why/What/Do/Read/Limits/What-to-read-next/Reproduce shape, every fitted example shrunk to render in under two minutes, captioned colourblind-safe ggplot2 figures in place of base graphics, tables through knitr::kable(), and a stated limit that the random-effects lenses’ fixed N(0, 5) coefficient prior dominates on raw-scale (tens- or hundreds-scale) responses unless the caller standardises the response and covariates before building the pass.
  • Fix: synthesise() no longer silently drops a lens that abstains at fit time. Previously the fit-time koine_abstention a lens returns had no $status field, so the “contributed” filter dropped it without recording why, and the synthesis-level abstention then blamed the PSIS gate (psis_unreliable) even when no lens ever reached it. The lens’s real reason (e.g. convergence_failed, feature_unsupported) now propagates to the synthesis-level reason when it is the sole distinct reason among the declining lenses, and every declining lens is carried into lenses_dropped with that reason.
  • inst/INTEGRATION.md refreshed to describe the MET random-effects structure (two crossed/nested intercepts) as in-corner, add the groups argument to the IR-mapping table, and correct the stale version/licence status block.
  • Corrected a licence-metadata contradiction: README.md and CITATION.cff previously stated no licence was declared and the package was undistributed, while DESCRIPTION has declared MIT + file LICENSE since 2026-06-08 and the package is pushed to max578/koine. Both now state MIT and the correct installation/contributing instructions.
  • Corrected the RE-unsupported synthesis abstention’s detail text, which described the supported corner as “a single random intercept on one grouping factor” – stale since the MET (two crossed/nested intercepts) structure landed at 0.3.0. It now names both supported shapes.
  • Corrected a stale sentence in the koine: the synthesised fourth opinion vignette that described the Poisson GLMM lens as “held experimental pending a better-mixing sampler”; it has been enrolled (with a post-fit convergence gate) since 0.2.0.
  • Typeset the MET marginal-covariance equation in the vignette as LaTeX maths (previously inline code) and added two captioned, interpreted figures: the two-lens stacking-weight simplex with n_eff annotated, and the over-dispersed linear-pool envelope against the fitted data.
  • Replaced the em dash (---) with the house en dash (--) throughout README.md and the vignette prose.
  • Added @references (Vehtari, Simpson, Gelman, Yao & Gabry 2024 for the PSIS gate; Yao, Vehtari, Simpson & Gelman 2018 for the stacking objective) and an @examples block for is_abstention().
  • Fixed the new metadata-consistency test (README/CITATION.cff licence wording) failing with an error, rather than skipping, under R CMD check, where the source-tree files it reads are not installed alongside the package.
  • Corrected CONTRIBUTING.md’s stale instruction to branch off a dev branch that does not exist in this repository; it now says main.
  • Added inst/CITATION, so citation("koine") returns a reference.

koine 0.3.0

New features

  • The breeder-standard multi-environment-trial (MET) random-effects structure is now supported: two crossed or nested random intercepts, a variety effect and a trial (environment) effect, (1 | variety) + (1 | trial). koine now corroborates a production MET model directly — on the variety-plus-trial structure the production model actually fits — rather than on a single-random-effect reduction that discards the trial structure. Whether the two groupings are crossed or nested is resolved from the data, never from the formula.
  • The MET marginal stays exact for the Gaussian LMM: with two crossed groupings the marginal covariance is dense, so the single-random-intercept per-group quadrature no longer applies, but the marginal is still the exact multivariate normal y ~ N(X beta, sigma^2 I + tau_variety^2 Z_variety Z_variety' + tau_trial^2 Z_trial Z_trial'). fit_glmm_marginal() samples (beta, sigma, tau_variety, tau_trial) on that exact marginal (a dense Cholesky of V) with a coordinate-wise slice kernel, integrating the random effects out where the sealed engines sample or Laplace-approximate them. The exact marginal log-likelihood was validated to machine precision against an independent lme4 ML fit (the Independent Oracle Principle), and the MET fit concords with the NIMBLE MET reference (which samples the two crossed random effects). The draws now carry one tau_<grouping> per random factor.
  • The lift is additive. The single-random-intercept path (1 | g) is unchanged (byte-identical code path and accessors); the MET structure is the new capability, dispatched only when two groupings are present. No exported function gained or changed a required argument, so the public API and the C1/C3 triangulation contract hold. koine_pass_from_design() gained a groups argument (a named list of two grouping vectors) alongside the existing group.
  • A non-Gaussian MET — whose dense crossed-GLMM marginal has no exact quadrature — returns a lens-scope abstention (feature_unsupported) rather than an ungrounded approximation; the single-random-intercept GLMM path (Gaussian, binomial, Poisson) is untouched. The heavy-tailed single-RE lens (fit_glmm_robust_re()) is excluded from a MET pass with a recorded reason rather than dropping the second grouping.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • The closed abstention taxonomy gained two fact-grounding reasons, data_ungrounded and provenance_unverified (Independent Oracle Principle). A converged, high-ESS lens fit on an ungrounded input still carries that input’s ungroundedness; these let a lens decline on a fact failure (an input marked ungrounded in the orchestra provenance vocabulary), not only on the existing numerical failures (convergence, calibration, ESS).
  • Fixed a latent NIMBLE compile failure for an intercept-only fixed part (K = 1). NIMBLE’s inprod() over a length-1 vector generates non-compiling Eigen C++, so the NIMBLE GLMM lenses now write the K = 1 fixed-effects mean as the scalar beta[1] and keep inprod() for K >= 2. The bug never fired before because every test used a K = 2 fixed part; the MET model (a commonly intercept-only fixed part) surfaced it.

koine 0.2.0

  • The Poisson GLMM (single random intercept, log link) is now ENROLLED for the marginal mixed-model lens (fit_glmm_marginal) and the NIMBLE reference lens (fit_nimble_glmm), validated by simulation-based calibration (SBC clean over the contributing simulations: every parameter’s rank uniform, p > 0.16) and cross-engine concordance against NIMBLE (median standardised discrepancy 0.23, SD ratios 0.94–1.17) on the identifiable-variance-component regime.
  • The Poisson marginal is sampled by a funnel-safe blocked slice kernel: log tau is slice-sampled, and the coefficients are slice-sampled along their tau-resolved principal axes (the scaled eigenvectors of the Laplace covariance of the coefficient conditional). This clears the variance-component funnel neck where a static-metric Hamiltonian kernel funnels (~50% divergences, ess_tau ~ 3) and a Laplace independence proposal freezes; the Gaussian and binomial marginals keep the joint NUTS kernel. A value-only marginal log-posterior (.glmm_marginal_logpost_value) backs the slice kernel (it skips the score- identity gradient quadrature the slice never uses).
  • At a large random-intercept SD (tau beyond ~2, the ~8% upper tail of the prior) the marginalised funnel is too weakly identified for any marginal sampler to mix — with the random effects integrated out, the non-centred remedy is unavailable. A post-fit convergence gate makes the lens ABSTAIN (convergence_failed, a new first-class abstention reason — too few effective draws or chains that disagree) rather than contribute a badly-mixed opinion. koine contributes a calibrated Poisson opinion where the variance component is identifiable, and abstains where it is not (a first-class outcome, SS3).

koine 0.1.1

  • koine_opinion_draws() now mixes each parameter only over the lenses for which it is comparable: the linear-predictor coefficients over every contributing lens, but a scale parameter (sigma, tau) only over the family-likelihood lenses. A likelihood-variant lens (the robust-t lens, which carries its own Student-t likelihood) reports its scale on a different metric (a Student-t scale rather than a Gaussian SD), so it is excluded from the scale mixture — and flagged in the new koine_scale_restricted attribute — while still contributing to the coefficients. This fixes a synthesised-sigma bias when a likelihood-variant lens carried stacking weight (it dragged sigma toward the t-scale); the fixed effects are unchanged. The draws are a per-parameter marginal representation, which is what a parameter-marginal triangulation needs.

koine 0.1.0

First tagged release — the version carrying the IR-targetable, re-entrant model builder (koine_pass_from_design()) and the integration surface a parent triangulation panel drives, so koine clears the backend contract’s construction, output, and determinism clauses. Licence declared MIT.

Stage-2 — random-effects support (single random intercept)

  • koine_pass() now parses an lme4-style random intercept (1 | g) on one grouping factor into a fixed-effects design plus a random-effects design; richer structure (random slopes, multiple or crossed/nested groupings) is parsed and flagged unsupported so the battery abstains (feature_unsupported) rather than silently fitting the wrong model. This also closes a latent gap whereby a random-effects formula previously slipped through as a wrongly parsed population model.
  • resolve_battery() gained the feature-support gate (a lens enrols only when its random-effects support matches the pass), with directional recorded reasons.
  • Two orthogonal mixed-model lenses, stacked on the identical per-observation integrated predictive (the random effect marginalised under each draw’s variance components, so PSIS stays in its reliable regime): fit_glmm_marginal() — a koine-authored No-U-Turn (Hamiltonian) sampler that integrates the random effects out (exact for the Gaussian LMM, adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for a GLMM) and rides the marginal’s analytic gradient (the score identity for a GLMM, closed form for the Gaussian) — and fit_nimble_glmm() — NIMBLE Gibbs that samples the random effects. The two carry identical priors, so their agreement is method-independent consensus. Enrolled (validated) for the Gaussian LMM and the binomial GLMM (the Poisson GLMM is implemented but held experimental — see below).
  • A heavy-tailed random-effect lens, fit_glmm_robust_re(): a Gaussian LMM whose random intercepts are Student-t (b_g ~ t_nu), integrated out via the Normal scale-mixture (Gauss-Laguerre over the mixing scale). It is enrolled as a spectrum over the degrees of freedom (a grid nu in {3, 8}, analogous to the shrinkage spectrum), so stacking can favour the random-effect tail-weight the data support. It is the within-battery analogue of the population robust-t lens — where the Gaussian-RE lenses corroborate (weights collapse), the t-RE lenses earn real stacking weight when group effects are heavy-tailed (n_eff ~ 1.75 on t_3 effects), so koine’s RE opinion becomes sensitive to random-effect structure rather than a weighted echo of one assumption.
  • Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for the non-Gaussian random-effect marginal (per-group Newton mode-finding + curvature-scaled nodes, closed-form canonical-link scores added to family_spec). Fixed Gauss-Hermite is non-convergent for the sharply-peaked Poisson count integrand; adaptive Gauss-Hermite is accurate to ~1e-3 across the prior range and makes the binomial GLMM validate more accurately.
  • Family-appropriate weakly-informative priors (.re_prior()): the log-link Poisson uses a tighter coefficient / random-intercept-SD prior than the Gaussian and binomial families, whose N(0, 5) prior is fine.
  • assemble_loglik() and evidence_axis() gained random-effects branches built on a single shared marginalisation core.
  • A NaN-safe sampler guard: .dram_one_chain() and the marginal log-posteriors guard both Metropolis acceptance ratios against non-finite log-posteriors, so an extreme proposal is rejected (and a chain started from an impossible point escapes) rather than halting on a NaN acceptance test. Finite cases are unchanged.
  • The validation harness covers every mixed-model lens; the enrolled ones are validated by SBC plus cross-implementation concordance against NIMBLE (recorded study in inst/validation/). The Poisson GLMM remains held experimental and is not enrolled. The Hamiltonian kernel fixes the count-intercept mixing that the random walk could not (the original failure), but a minority of prior-plausible datasets with a large random-intercept SD give the marginal a variance-component funnel that a static-metric sampler cannot traverse cheaply (occasional divergences and order-minutes fits). Because the random effects are marginalised, the usual non-centred remedy does not apply; the recorded next step is a funnel-robust metric (Riemannian / Fisher information, reused from the quadrature) or a bounded enrolled-tau range.
  • koine_pass_from_design() — an IR-targetable, re-entrant, deparse-free model builder that constructs a pass directly from a named design matrix, a response, a family, and an optional grouping vector (no model formula, no match.call() capture, no session-global state). This is the programmatic entry a parent triangulation panel drives (the backend contract’s construction clause); it preserves non-syntactic canonical column names such as (Intercept) verbatim.
  • Integration surface for a parent triangulation panel (the contract is in inst/INTEGRATION.md): koine_opinion_draws() materialises the single synthesised opinion as a posterior draws_array over the parameters its contributing lenses share, sampling each lens in proportion to its stacking weight (a mixture over koine’s own battery, with the stacking weights and stacked predictive elpd surfaced as attributes — never a pool across the parent’s independent engines). synthesise() gains keep_fits to retain the per-lens fits for it, and koine_can_contribute() is a cheap pre-flight capability predicate for the parent’s backend-availability gate.

Stage-1 — the synthesis spine

First development scaffold — the Stage-1 increment-1 spine.

  • The engine-neutral request (koine_pass()) with content-hashed provenance, the evaluable family adapter (as_family_spec(), Gaussian / Binomial / Poisson), and the uniform lens-output contract (fb_fit()) with a complete, validated provenance record.

  • The enrolment registry and family-conditional resolve_battery() for the leanest Stage-1 cut (DRAM, NIMBLE-Gibbs, Polya-Gamma Gibbs, DREAM); only the DRAM lens carries a working adapter in this increment, the other three are registered but excluded with a recorded reason.

  • The first opinion lens: a self-contained, koine-authored delayed-rejection adaptive Metropolis sampler (fit_dram()).

  • The synthesis spine: pointwise log-likelihood assembly (assemble_loglik()), the tier-1 PSIS reliability gate (gate_psis()), predictive-space LOO-stacking (stack_opinion()), and the top-level synthesise() — which returns a first-class abstention when fewer than two independent opinion lenses survive.

  • The dual-reader NetCDF interchange (read_idata_nc(), RNetCDF canonical with an ncdf4 fallback), enforcing the four hard read assertions.

  • Abstention (abstention()) and the typed error taxonomy as first-class outcomes.

  • The full Stage-1 battery across three diversity axes: four inference-family witnesses (DRAM, NIMBLE-Gibbs, Polya-Gamma Gibbs, DREAM_ZS), a heavy-tail structure variant (fit_robust_t()), and a shrinkage spectrum (fit_ridge() / fit_lasso() / fit_horseshoe()), with the weight-concentration diagnostic and the weight_degenerate abstention.

  • The diagnostic layer is complete: alongside weight concentration, linear_pool_envelope() reports an over-dispersed reference bracket and flags disagreeing lenses leave-one-out, and evidence_axis() reports per-lens marginal likelihoods (bridge sampling, prior-conditional). Both carry role = "diagnostic" and are surfaced by synthesise(), never pooled into the opinion.

  • A validation / maturity gate for koine-authored lenses (the open-arms correctness obligation): simulation-based calibration (sbc_check()), an exact grid-based reference-posterior check (reference_posterior_check()), and the corroboration gate (gate_corroboration()). resolve_battery() now excludes a koine-first lens until its validation evidence is on record — an unvalidated first-mover abstains. The DRAM, Polya-Gamma Gibbs, and robust-t lenses are validated (the recorded study is in inst/validation/).

  • Release-grade documentation and tooling: a runnable @examples block on every exported function, an en-GB spell-check gate (inst/WORDLIST), a pkgdown site, a README, a CITATION.cff, an air.toml / .lintr style configuration, and an R-CMD-check GitHub Actions workflow. R CMD check --as-cran is clean (no ERRORs or WARNINGs).

No licence is declared yet (pending the required consultation); the package is local-only and not distributed.
